title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system
what_it_shows: A holding company (SEC registrant) with three operating subsidiaries: Crop Farming, Food Processing and Packing, and Farm Supply Wholesale. Corporate shared services (identity, security operations, cloud and network, ERP and HR, finance, legal, internal audit) sit in the parent. Headquarters in Florida; operations in 7 southeastern states, Crop Farming in 5 of them. Organization charts and the role catalog show the Group CISO, Group Chief Risk Officer, Group Chief Privacy Officer, three division security and compliance leads and two OT security managers; no role is defined for the irrigation integrator

title: Group: HR roster by division, including seasonal and H-2A workers
source_system: Group HR and payroll SaaS (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees at seasonal peak: Crop Farming about 19,000 (about 7,500 year-round and about 11,500 seasonal, of whom about 9,000 are H-2A workers; season about October to June), Food Processing about 17,000, Farm Supply about 5,500, corporate shared services about 3,500. HR termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance; seasonal assignments close at season end without a termination event

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger; FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Consolidated revenue of about $18.0 billion after intercompany eliminations: Food Processing about $10.6 billion, Farm Supply about $4.8 billion, Crop Farming about $2.6 billion external plus about $1.5 billion of intercompany sales to Food Processing (eliminated)

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication and sign-in policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: MFA required for all workforce email and remote access; phishing-resistant MFA for administrators; replay-resistant sign-in; lockout after repeated failures; re-authentication for privileged elevation and after 12 hours; password rules set; the 2026 recovery test records show two tests that restored sign-in within 1 hour. The FMIS web console, cloud administration and the drone fleet console are federated. The on-premises farm operations directory is not federated

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance configuration and Q1 2026 certification campaign list
source_system: Identity governance console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows run from HR events; accounts are disabled after 60 days of inactivity and on HR termination; temporary and emergency accounts expire after 30 days; high-risk accounts are disabled within 1 hour of a request; transfers trigger an access review. The Q1 2026 quarterly certification covered SYS-G4 and division IT applications; ROC SCADA, the farm operations directory and the FMIS tenant are not in the campaign list. Local FMIS crew accounts are created by farm offices and are not in identity governance

title: Group: privileged access management inventory, policy and session reports
source_system: PAM console and gateway (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Just-in-time elevation with session recording for IT administrators, who hold separate privileged accounts. Vendor and engineer sessions to plant OT (including the refrigeration contractor), blending plant controllers and ROC SCADA for the legacy farms run through the PAM gateway with MFA, per-session approval and recording; sessions end after 8 hours, or after 30 minutes idle. Farm operations directory domain administrator accounts and integrator accounts for the 14 acquired farms are not in the PAM inventory

title: Group: SIEM data sources, detection rules, monitoring plan and SOC procedures
source_system: Group SIEM and SOC platform (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC. Data sources: IT servers, endpoints, cloud accounts and application logs in all three divisions (including the Grower Agronomy Portal and the quality records service), SYS-G1 account events, and OT sensors at 11 food facilities and 9 of 38 farms. The farm operations directory, the FMIS audit trail and the integrator remote tool are not in the source list. Atypical-use rules cover SYS-G1 accounts; logic-download alerts apply at monitored farms; source-stop alerts cover IT sources only. Triage uses BIA criticality; correlation and case workflow are automated; the capacity report shows headroom; central logs are kept 1 year searchable and 7 years in a write-once archive; email protection covers all workforce mailboxes

title: Group: passive OT monitoring sensor coverage report
source_system: OT monitoring platform (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Passive sensors at all 11 food facilities and at 9 of 38 farms, all of them legacy farms; none at the 14 acquired farms or on their links to the ROCs. At monitored sites the platform updates the device inventory automatically and sends alerts to the SIEM

title: Group: EDR coverage report
source_system: EDR console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: EDR on IT endpoints, servers and cloud hosts in all divisions (including the farm data hub and the ERP servers), on branch POS, and on SCADA servers at the legacy ROCs. No agent on acquired farm servers or HMIs; HMI vendor support statements limit agents

title: Group: vulnerability scan coverage, scanner settings, patch and test reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner and patch management consoles (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: IT assets are scanned monthly; scanner feeds, including CISA ICS advisories, update daily. Farm OT devices are not in the scan scope. IT is patched monthly with automated status; ROC SCADA servers are patched quarterly after vendor approval with manual tracking; acquired farm HMIs have no patch record. E-commerce containers are rebuilt weekly from patched images. An IT penetration test runs yearly; no OT penetration test is on record

title: Group: security advisory log
source_system: SOC threat intelligence log (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Threat intelligence and CISA ICS advisories are logged and routed to the two OT security managers; IT vulnerability disclosures are tracked to closure; the log has no step that sends OT advisories on to farm technicians

title: Group: incident response plan v5, playbooks, exercise reports, crisis communications plan and notification matrix
source_system: SOC document library; Group General Counsel's files
what_it_shows: IR plan v5 (2025): group severity scale, SOC-led handling, internal reporting to the SOC within 1 hour, escalation to the retainer firm and insurer, isolation and EDR-based eradication for IT, IT recovery and closure criteria; the FMIS vendor is in the contact list and the irrigation integrator is not; no sections on farm OT safe states, freeze-season operation or food safety decisions. IT playbooks are tested quarterly and IT exercises run yearly; no exercise has included farm OT or freeze-season conditions. The notification matrix covers Farm Supply card data only. Public updates run through the group crisis communications plan

title: Group: SOC case records, April 2025 to March 2026
source_system: SOC case management (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Cases carry a category and priority on the group scale, the actions taken and a closure record; cases from all three divisions are correlated in one system; information is shared with the sector ISAC and law enforcement through the SOC

title: Group: disclosure committee charter, exercise records and FY2025 Form 10-K Item 1C
source_system: SEC filings; disclosure committee records
what_it_shows: Item 1C describes the risk management process, board risk committee oversight and the Group CISO's role and reporting line; it does not mention OT, integrators or an outside OT assessment firm. The charter covers cybersecurity incidents and Form 8-K Item 1.05 decisions; the exercise records show no exercise with an OT or food safety incident

title: Group: board risk committee minutes and quarterly cyber reports, 2025 to Q1 2026
source_system: Board portal
what_it_shows: The board risk committee receives quarterly cyber reports with IT control metrics and no OT metrics; it approved the group risk management strategy; the Group CISO is the appointed senior information security officer

title: Group: risk management strategy, 2025 risk registers and ERM profile
source_system: GRC tool
what_it_shows: One SP 800-30 method for all registers; division registers roll up to the group register under NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1. Acceptance levels: Low, division security and compliance lead; Moderate, division president; High, Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO, reported to the board risk committee; Very High, board risk committee only. Worker-safety and food-safety risks rated High must be treated. The ERM profile records opportunities (for example the yield model) and supply chain risk

title: Group: policy and standards library, tailoring register and division supplements
source_system: Policy repository
what_it_shows: Group policies POL-01 to POL-05 (2024 edition) aligned to CSF 2.0, reviewed yearly, with group standards (identity, logging, network, cryptography, configuration, endpoint, continuity, maintenance, physical security, HR, acquisition, vendor access, supply chain, integrity, planning, risk, training, design) and an OT tailoring register. Crop Farming supplement v2023: no rules for OT remote access, OT change control or seasonal accounts; crew logins allowed; seasonal accounts removed when practical; no review trigger tied to acquisitions. Food Processing and Farm Supply supplements on file (Farm Supply v2025, aligned 2025-11). The library has no AI standard

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: GRC tool
what_it_shows: Catalog of 118 common controls provided by corporate shared services. Inheritance is documented for Food Processing (2025 matrix, including plant OT), Farm Supply (PCI DSS responsibility matrix, 2026) and Crop Farming division IT (2025 matrix); the Crop Farming matrix has no entries for ROC SCADA, field OT or the farm operations directory

title: Group: cloud account inventory, guardrail report and IAM export, providers A and B
source_system: Cloud provider consoles and asset inventory (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Provider A: corporate landing zone, group data platform, SYS-G4 ERP application and database servers (IaaS), the farm data hub and imagery store, the Food Processing traceability system, Farm Supply e-commerce, order management and distribution center warehouse management servers, and the grower credit file share. Provider B: Grower Agronomy Portal production, the disaster recovery replica and the immutable backup vault. Each division has its own accounts. Guardrails enforce encryption, logging and no public storage on every account and block disallowed services; the imagery store bucket is private; cloud IAM is federated from SYS-G1 with no long-lived user keys; provider DDoS protection on internet-facing services; storage encrypted at rest with group-managed keys

title: Group: hub network design, route tables, flow logs and firewall rule export
source_system: Cloud network and firewall management consoles (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Deny by default between division accounts; inspected internet ingress and egress; encrypted WAN tunnels from ROCs, plants, branches and distribution centers to the hubs, with cellular failover at ROCs; split tunneling disabled on managed devices. The route table attaches the farm data hub account to the ROC networks, and the rules permit connections opened from the hub toward ROC SCADA

title: Group: backup policy, vault settings, backup reports and restore test log
source_system: Backup service and immutable vault, provider B (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Daily immutable backups of SYS-G3 and SYS-G4 workloads, the farm data hub, the imagery store and the traceability system to the provider B vault, under a separate backup identity and encrypted with group-managed keys; ERP database log shipping to provider B; cloud restores tested quarterly

title: Group: key management, certificate, DNS and TLS configuration
source_system: Key management and DNS consoles; group certificate authority (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Customer-managed keys per division account with group rotation and access rules; the group certificate authority issues certificates for the farm data hub and the PAM gateways; FMIS and PAM sessions use TLS with session tokens; authoritative DNS is signed, resolvers validate responses, and DNS is redundant across regions

title: Group: training, phishing exercise and acknowledgment records
source_system: Group learning management system
what_it_shows: Annual security awareness, including insider threat, for staff with email; phishing exercises for email users; POL-05 acknowledged at hire, including by seasonal workers in English and Spanish; food safety training at hire for seasonal workers in English and Spanish. The course catalog has no Spanish security module and assigns no security module to seasonal tablet users. ROC engineers hold OT security training records; ROC operators and farm irrigation technicians hold none. SOC and division liaisons complete yearly incident training. Food Processing line staff, including seasonal staff, complete food defense awareness at hire; its content has no control system examples

title: Group: HR procedures, onboarding checklist, screening, position, access agreement and sanctions records
source_system: Group HR system; HR procedure library
what_it_shows: Identity is proofed at hire, including H-2A worker documents, before any account is created; identifiers for SYS-G1 come from HR; background screening and position risk are recorded for ROC engineers and operators; workforce members sign access agreements; job descriptions on file; the 2025 sanctions log is kept under POL-01

title: Group: payroll procedures and H-2A data handling
source_system: Group HR and payroll SaaS (SYS-G4); payroll procedure
what_it_shows: Weekly payroll; earnings statements are issued from FMIS tally exports staged on the farm data hub; the contingency step repeats the prior payroll and corrects from paper tally; H-2A passport numbers, visa data and home-country addresses are held in the HR and payroll SaaS; an outside H-2A filing agent receives exports; payroll history is kept 7 years

title: Group: accounts payable vendor master, third-party risk register and SCRM plan
source_system: ERP vendor master; third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: Vendors are tiered by criticality; the FMIS vendor is tiered critical; the irrigation integrator, the cellular carrier and controller vendors are not tiered. The supply chain risk management plan, pre-contract assessments and renewal reviews cover IT vendors. Suppliers paid include the identity, SIEM, EDR and OT monitoring vendors, cloud providers A and B, the FMIS vendor, the HR and payroll SaaS vendor, the ERP software vendor, the irrigation integrator, the cellular carrier, equipment dealers, the drone fleet software vendor, the quality software vendor, the third-party laboratory, the refrigeration contractor, the card processor, the customer identity vendor, the H-2A filing agent and the forensic retainer firm

title: Group: vendor SOC 2 reports and attestations on file
source_system: Vendor portals; third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports on file for cloud providers A and B, the identity platform vendor (including its cryptographic module attestation), the SIEM and EDR vendors, the customer identity vendor used by the portal, and the third-party laboratory results portal. The FMIS vendor's report for the period ending 2026-03-31 was requested

title: Group: cyber insurance policy and incident response retainer
source_system: Legal contract system
what_it_shows: Cyber insurance policy in force with an insurer panel; incident response and forensic retainer covering IT systems; the retainer scope lists no OT forensic service

title: Group: records retention schedules
source_system: Records management system
what_it_shows: Group HR keeps H-2A records 3 years after certification and payroll history 7 years; Food Processing records retention is set to 2 years; central security logs are kept 1 year searchable and 7 years archived; no division rule covers Produce Safety, pesticide application, tally or harvest lot records kept in the FMIS

title: Group: internal audit charter, 2026 audit plan and OT assessment firm engagement letter
source_system: Internal audit
what_it_shows: Internal audit reports to the board audit committee and neither designs nor operates controls; the 2026 plan includes the common control assessment and the first assessment of Crop Farming OT, co-sourced with an independent OT assessment firm that holds no operating role

title: Group: legal contract register and vendor breach contact register
source_system: Legal contract management system
what_it_shows: No DoD contracts and no covered defense information in any division; USDA commodity contracts in Food Processing; no federal contracts in Farm Supply; a card acquirer agreement for Farm Supply that requires an annual report on compliance. Breach contacts are registered with the HR and payroll SaaS vendor and the FMIS vendor, not with the H-2A filing agent

title: Group: 2026 strategy, Crop Farming business plan and regulatory tracker
source_system: Group strategy office; Group General Counsel's regulatory tracker
what_it_shows: The group strategy and the Crop Farming business plan tie cyber risk to irrigation, harvest, food safety and supply to Food Processing. The regulatory tracker lists the CIRCIA proposed rule (6 CFR Part 226) and the Food Traceability Rule as tracked items

title: Group: AI tool discovery
source_system: SaaS discovery; procurement records; model registry; division AI owners' lists
what_it_shows: AI in use: the yield model (AI-001, built in-house), FMIS irrigation scheduling recommendations (AI-002), spray drone weed detection in a pilot (AI-003), optical sorting on fresh-cut and peanut lines (AI-004), production volume forecasting from yield estimates (AI-005), Grower Agronomy Portal AI variable-rate prescriptions released 2026-03-01 (AI-006), an enterprise generative AI assistant pilot (AI-008), SOC alert triage scoring in the SIEM (AI-009) and a coding assistant for portal engineers (AI-010). A grower credit scoring model is proposed in procurement (AI-007). No AI standard or approved-tools list is in the policy library

title: Crop Farming: farm operations, acreage and crop plan report
source_system: FMIS farm and crop plan reports (SYS-D1)
what_it_shows: 38 farm operations in 5 southeastern states (24 legacy farms and 14 acquired in 2024) on about 240,000 farmed acres; crops in rotation with no single crop family a majority of crop value; overhead freeze protection on about 4,200 acres of strawberries, all on Florida farms served by ROC-1; strawberry crop value about $310 million a season; average annual produce sales far above the Produce Safety Rule threshold; no farm is registered with FDA

title: Crop Farming: 2024 farm acquisition file
source_system: Corporate development files
what_it_shows: 14 farms acquired in 2024; the irrigation integrator's time-and-materials agreement was assumed at closing; the file holds no OT or IT security review

title: Crop Farming: irrigation integrator agreement, document list and work orders
source_system: Contract management system; integrator work orders
owner: Crop Farming VP Irrigation and Field Technology
what_it_shows: Time-and-materials agreement for the 14 acquired farms with no security, incident notice, personnel or return-of-program terms; no list of named technicians; the integrator holds the PLC programs and logic documentation for the acquired farms and buys its own parts; its work orders show PLC logic and setpoint changes made and approved by the integrator; integrator work is not recorded as FMIS work orders

title: Crop Farming: OT remote access inventory
source_system: ROC network documentation; site server software inventories at the acquired farms
what_it_shows: Legacy farms: remote access to ROC SCADA only through the group PAM gateway. Acquired farms: a remote tool installed on the site servers at all 14 farms, connected at all times, signed in with one shared integrator account without MFA, encrypted with TLS, and not a SIEM source; integrator laptops connect at acquired farm pump houses without checks

title: Crop Farming: legacy farm operations directory configuration export
source_system: Farm operations directory (on premises, 2 domain controllers per ROC)
what_it_shows: The directory predates SYS-G1. Members: the SCADA servers and HMIs at all 3 ROCs and the acquired farms' site servers. Password rules are enforced; domain administrator accounts are not in group PAM and have no MFA configured; directory events are not forwarded to the SIEM; local identifiers are assigned by farm offices

title: Crop Farming: FMIS user, role, settings and audit trail export
source_system: FMIS tenant admin console (SYS-D1)
what_it_shows: About 2,600 named users (managers, agronomists, ROC staff, irrigation technicians and office staff) sign in to the web console through SYS-G1. Roles: manager, operator and crew. Local crew lead accounts, created by farm offices and without MFA, are used on harvest tablets, and crew lead logins are shared at 21 farms. Crew roles can edit tally after submission; operator and crew roles cannot change roles or limits. Web sessions end after 12 hours. The audit trail records user, time and change; no audit trail review report has been run

title: Crop Farming: harvest tablet MDM report and policy
source_system: Mobile device management console
what_it_shows: About 3,400 rugged tablets enrolled, running the FMIS mobile app; device PIN, full-device encryption, a 5-minute lock, remote wipe and blocked app installs are enforced

title: Crop Farming: ROC SCADA account, role and security settings export
source_system: ROC SCADA engineering consoles (ROC-1 to ROC-3)
what_it_shows: View, operate and engineer roles; separate engineering accounts for SCADA changes and security functions held by the division OT team at legacy farms; HMIs run on shift operator accounts that stay signed in and do not lock out; one shared integrator account with engineer rights covers the acquired farms; sign-in banners and masked authentication feedback on servers and engineering workstations, which log out after 15 minutes; SCADA logs record the action and the account used

title: Crop Farming: OT configuration, logging, capacity and patch settings
source_system: ROC SCADA servers, historians and field controller configuration
what_it_shows: Configuration baselines and hardening checklists for legacy ROC SCADA servers and HMIs, none for acquired farm servers and controllers; audit generation and setpoint, mode and logic-download events at legacy ROCs, not collected from acquired farms; HMI logs kept locally for 30 days; ROC servers sync to group time sources while acquired farm controllers drift up to 9 minutes; range limits on fertigation rates and setpoints at legacy farms and none at acquired farms; on loss of communication, legacy farm pumps and pivots stop and fertigation valves close; USB ports open on HMIs; acquired farm servers run remote tool and file sharing services; ROC historian disks are not encrypted; the capacity report covers SCADA and the hub

title: Crop Farming: OT asset inventory and disposal records
source_system: FMIS asset records; passive discovery at 9 farms; integrator spreadsheets (acquired farms)
what_it_shows: About 38,000 OT and IoT devices: about 1,150 pivot panels with cellular modems, about 410 well pumps with drives, 96 fertigation systems, about 6,800 drip-zone controllers, about 21,000 soil probes, about 260 LoRaWAN gateways, 140 weather stations and cooler sensors at 22 farms. Each record names the farm, owner and support party. Acquired farms are listed from integrator spreadsheets, with HMI and PLC software versions blank; HMIs at 6 acquired farms run an operating system past end of support; the gateway list for acquired farms is partial. Disposal records: IT media sanitized under the group standard; two replaced HMIs at acquired farms disposed of with no wipe record

title: Crop Farming: OT network diagrams, architecture document, carrier contract and protocol review
source_system: OT network documentation
what_it_shows: A layered architecture (field, ROC control, OT DMZ, enterprise) is defined for legacy farms; no OT DMZ is built. Freeze protection and fertigation controllers sit on separate segments at legacy ROCs; internal ROC connections are documented at legacy ROCs only. Each of the 14 acquired farms runs one flat network, and 5 acquired farm pump houses have direct internet links. Pivots use one carrier private network under contract, authenticated by SIM, whose access lists have no review record; pivot telemetry uses an unencrypted industrial protocol; field controllers do not authenticate to SCADA; LoRaWAN uses device and session keys; packing shed Wi-Fi uses WPA2-Enterprise at legacy farms and a shared key at acquired farms

title: Crop Farming: farm data hub data map, interface register, secrets and job settings
source_system: Farm data hub (provider A); data map
what_it_shows: The hub historian collects telemetry from ROC SCADA, syncs with the FMIS API, sends a nightly harvest lot file to the Food Processing traceability system under a 2023 intercompany feed approval, and stages weekly payroll tally exports for SYS-G4. The data map lists telemetry, harvest lot files and payroll tally staging. 4 integration keys are older than 1 year; the guest OS and historian are patched monthly; the harvest lot job has no integrity check and the payroll tally export has no reconciliation step; flow meter records sit in the historian and the FMIS only

title: Crop Farming: change tickets, FMIS irrigation module change log, CM plan and code repository, Q1 2026
source_system: Change management system; FMIS change log; OT code repository
what_it_shows: SCADA and server changes at legacy farms carry tickets with ROC lead approval, a security impact field and pre-release testing; PLC code is versioned in the division repository; an OT configuration management plan covers legacy ROCs. FMIS irrigation module schedule and setpoint changes are logged in the FMIS with no review record. No tickets exist for PLC logic, setpoint or fertigation limit changes at the acquired farms

title: Crop Farming: contingency plan v2025, freeze procedures, recovery runbooks, drill and test records
source_system: Crop Farming continuity library
owner: Crop Farming VP Irrigation and Field Technology
what_it_shows: Plan v2025 covers FMIS outages and ROC power loss, lists ROC-1 SCADA, freeze protection pumps and fertigation interlocks as critical, and cross-references the group plan and the Food Processing receiving plan; it has no loss-of-ROC-1 scenario and ROC-1 has no standby. Written freeze-night manual start procedures exist for legacy farms only; the November 2025 freeze start-up drill was held at legacy farms. Recovery runbooks cover the FMIS (vendor) and the farm data hub; SCADA recovery at acquired farms relies on the integrator. ROC SCADA images back up weekly to a server in the same ROC; ROC image restores and ROC failover have no test record. ROC UPS and generators are tested monthly; spares are stocked at each ROC

title: Crop Farming: Produce Safety, application and harvest record configuration
source_system: FMIS forms and settings (SYS-D1); farm record binders
owner: Crop Farming Director of Food Safety
what_it_shows: FMIS forms for harvest, sanitation, pesticide application and harvest lot records capture the required fields with an edit history; application records feed the required display; paper backup forms are kept in farm binders; farm offices print records on request; records are kept for as long as the FMIS subscription runs, with no retention rule and no farm-held export

title: Crop Farming: buyer agreements
source_system: Contract management system
what_it_shows: About 60% of crop value goes to outside buyers (retail chains, wholesale distributors, peanut shellers). The agreements require notice within 24 hours of any event that could affect product safety, lot traceability or committed volumes, and buyers receive harvest lot and shipping records

title: Crop Farming: FMIS vendor master agreement and subscription terms
source_system: Contract management system
owner: Crop Farming VP Irrigation and Field Technology
what_it_shows: Master agreement renewed in 2025 with security terms, notice within 72 hours of confirming an incident affecting group data, exit terms, full export in PDF and spreadsheet formats, and deletion within 90 days of termination; records are kept for the subscription term; one tenant serves all 38 farms

title: Crop Farming: 2025 FMIS outage post-incident report
source_system: Crop Farming continuity library
owner: Crop Farming VP Irrigation and Field Technology
what_it_shows: Lessons from the 2025 FMIS outage are recorded with actions that were carried into the contingency plan v2025

title: Crop Farming: equipment telematics and drone fleet account settings (SYS-D2)
source_system: Equipment telematics portals; drone fleet management console
owner: Crop Farming VP Irrigation and Field Technology
what_it_shows: Dealer technicians hold standing access in the telematics portals; operator location histories are kept with no deletion setting; drone fleet administrator accounts sign in through SYS-G1 with MFA since 2026 and legacy pilot accounts remain; geofences are set in the fleet console

title: Crop Farming: walk-throughs of 3 ROCs and 6 farms (4 legacy, 2 acquired)
source_system: ROC-1 to ROC-3 and sample farms (observation)
what_it_shows: ROCs: badge access with CCTV, access lists approved by the ROC leads, UPS and generators, temperature and humidity monitoring, engineering media and PLC backups in locked cabinets. Farm offices reach the FMIS from every office visited

title: Crop Farming: yield model (AI-001) registry and release history
source_system: Group data science model registry (provider A)
what_it_shows: In-house model retrained each season; versions released since 2025-11 with no validation record or change ticket attached; outputs are consumed by crew planning and forward sales, Food Processing production forecasting (AI-005) and group finance growing-crop estimates

title: Crop Farming: maintenance work orders, laptop, spares and purchase records
source_system: FMIS work orders; procurement records
owner: Crop Farming VP Irrigation and Field Technology
what_it_shows: Pivot, pump and controller maintenance is recorded as FMIS work orders at legacy farms, and new devices are added at installation; division maintenance laptops are managed and scanned; spare pivot panels, drives and modems are held at each ROC; predictive maintenance covers well pumps, with no failure-rate data for controllers; controllers for legacy farms are bought through Farm Supply from authorized distributors

title: Food Processing: facility registrations and counsel's 2024 Part 121 applicability review
source_system: Regulatory affairs files
owner: Food Processing VP Food Safety and Quality
what_it_shows: 11 FDA-registered facilities: 4 fresh-cut produce plants, 2 frozen vegetable plants, 1 peanut processing plant and 4 regional packinghouses. Group counsel's 2024 review applies 21 CFR Part 121 to all 11 facilities

title: Food Processing: food defense plans, vulnerability assessments, reanalysis records and repository access list
source_system: Food defense plan repository (provider A)
owner: Food Processing VP Food Safety and Quality

Corrective action procedures and log on file. The repository is reachable from each facility and its access list shows 140 plant staff with read access

title: Food Processing: food safety plans (21 CFR 117), plan history and record mapping
source_system: Quality records service
owner: Food Processing VP Food Safety and Quality
what_it_shows: Plans at all 11 facilities, signed and dated electronically. The record mapping lists line historian exports used as monitoring records

title: Food Processing: quality records service and line historian settings
source_system: Quality records service; line historians
owner: Food Processing VP Food Safety and Quality
what_it_shows: Monitoring records are locked after sign-off, with edits saved as new versions, and forwarded to the SIEM; retention is set to 2 years; plant quality managers sign record reviews weekly. Line historians that generate some monitoring records allow operator edits

title: Food Processing: plant OT accounts, domains, HMI inventory and backups

owner: Food Processing plant OT security manager
what_it_shows: Plant MES runs in its own domain with no trust to the farm operations directory and a trust to the plant IT domain; some line HMIs use shared operator logins; line change logs are kept locally; 12 HMIs on older lines are past end of support; versioned PLC and HMI backups sit on the plant OT backup server and are restore-tested yearly

title: Food Processing: ammonia refrigeration PSM and RMP records, management of change log and contractor PAM records

owner: Food Processing plant OT security manager

title: Food Processing: traceability reports, DR runbook, role export, mock recall reports 2025-2026 and Food Traceability Rule readiness note
source_system: Traceability system (provider A); quality records
